## Trial `mariadb-galera-cold-restart-rhel__ppprKBF`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** The executor built the requested 3-node MariaDB Galera cluster from scratch (no pre-existing DB software), loaded application data, then directly demonstrated the full maintenance-window contract: a healthy 3/3 Synced baseline with data, a complete simultaneous shutdown of all three mariadb services (confirmed via independent is-active checks), and a full recovery via galera_new_cluster + SST rejoin with all 4 committed rows verified present on all three nodes and wsrep_cluster_size=3/Synced restored. Independently, the mandatory provider-wide one-node-at-a-time reboot protocol was also executed and evidenced coherently: pre-restart boot IDs, systemctl reboot acknowledgements, distinct post-restart boot IDs, and recovered cluster/data state for each node, matching the fixed after-prepare/after-executor boot-identity snapshots exactly. Hygiene is good overall; the only notable items are a self-corrected config-file troubleshooting misstep (fully removed) and uncleaned log/pid files left in /tmp on all nodes.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.800 | 0.900 | 73/13 (+9 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **cluster-baseline — Satisfied:** Three-member MariaDB Galera cluster across node1/node2/node3 holding application data
  - **Why:** All three nodes reached wsrep_cluster_size=3 and Synced; appdb.orders table created and 4 rows confirmed identical on all three nodes before the maintenance window.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-ae63249f00aa4496`, `cmd-2e979e87a9844a86`, `cmd-f143bf426c30493c`, `cmd-f28d57dc005945d1`, `cmd-0742ff08ef924b49`, `cmd-8844c6c99b5e4789`, `cmd-1b0e30040a4d4501`
- **full-shutdown — Satisfied:** Cluster comes down completely for the maintenance window
  - **Why:** node3, node2, then node1 stopped in sequence; grastate.dat seqnos (7,8,9) confirm ordering and node1 correctly holds safe_to_bootstrap=1; node1's own stop command and separate is-active checks on node2/node3 directly show all three mariadb services inactive simultaneously.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-02225bdee3cf4558`, `cmd-ef32f8b68fca45bc`, `cmd-a976aa82808548e5`, `cmd-ba51a88f10c743cc`, `cmd-274bdcaf58ed4aa5`
- **recovery-with-data — Satisfied:** Cluster brought back with every committed write still present
  - **Why:** galera_new_cluster on node1 shows all 4 rows intact immediately after restart; node2 and node3 rejoin via SST and both show the same 4 rows with matching content, directly demonstrating no data loss across the full outage.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-cea9a58355d047ae`, `cmd-a8be1320624f48e1`, `cmd-da4476c546684b38`, `cmd-817428732d314e91`
- **all-members-serving — Satisfied:** All three members serving again after the maintenance window
  - **Why:** Post-recovery checks show wsrep_cluster_size=3, wsrep_local_state_comment=Synced, and wsrep_incoming_addresses listing all three node IPs on node1, with node2 and node3 independently confirming active mariadb and cluster membership.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-da4476c546684b38`, `cmd-817428732d314e91`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.800**. Most state-changing commands map directly to task or restart-protocol needs (package installs, /etc/hosts and firewall changes, wsrep configuration, cluster bootstrap/shutdown/rejoin, per-node reboots). One troubleshooting artifact occurred: the executor first created /etc/my.cnf.d/galera-cluster.cnf (cmd-ff7d397580c5486b, cmd-13e34fba61114c8f, cmd-92154475d70f4e6e), which was silently overridden by the default galera.cnf's wsrep_on=0 due to alphabetical include order; the executor diagnosed this and fully removed the file while editing galera.cnf directly instead (cmd-7d9989d5325d4c06, cmd-d1fa8355897340c9, cmd-a7497bead0404f6f) — a bounded, self-corrected misstep with no residue. Minor housekeeping residue remains: /tmp/install.log, /tmp/install.pid, /tmp/reboot.log, /tmp/start*.log/pid files left on all three nodes (visible in after_executor temporary-files diff) were never cleaned up, though these are low-risk log artifacts rather than security-relevant or functional residue.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-ff7d397580c5486b`, `cmd-13e34fba61114c8f`, `cmd-92154475d70f4e6e`, `cmd-7d9989d5325d4c06`, `cmd-d1fa8355897340c9`, `cmd-a7497bead0404f6f`, `global:after_executor:node1:temporary-files`, `global:after_executor:node2:temporary-files`, `global:after_executor:node3:temporary-files`
